numbering: Standard 700-verse canon; Chapter 13 has 34 verses and excludes Arjuna's alternate opening question.
sourceChapterWithLineNumbers:
1:   Arjuna.
2:   Lord! of the men who serve Thee--true in heart--
3:   As God revealed; and of the men who serve,
4:   Worshipping Thee Unrevealed, Unbodied, Far,
5:   Which take the better way of faith and life?
6: 
7:   Krishna.
8:   Whoever serve Me--as I show Myself--
9:   Constantly true, in full devotion fixed,
10:   Those hold I very holy. But who serve--
11:   Worshipping Me The One, The Invisible,
12:   The Unrevealed, Unnamed, Unthinkable,
13:   Uttermost, All-pervading, Highest, Sure--
14:   Who thus adore Me, mastering their sense,
15:   Of one set mind to all, glad in all good,
16:   These blessed souls come unto Me.
17: 
18:   Yet, hard
19:   The travail is for such as bend their minds
20:   To reach th' Unmanifest That viewless path
21:   Shall scarce be trod by man bearing the flesh!
22:   But whereso any doeth all his deeds
23:   Renouncing self for Me, full of Me, fixed
24:   To serve only the Highest, night and day
25:   Musing on Me--him will I swiftly lift
26:   Forth from life's ocean of distress and death,
27:   Whose soul clings fast to Me. Cling thou to Me!
28:   Clasp Me with heart and mind! so shalt thou dwell
29:   Surely with Me on high. But if thy thought
30:   Droops from such height; if thou be'st weak to set
31:   Body and soul upon Me constantly,
32:   Despair not! give Me lower service! seek
33:   To reach Me, worshipping with steadfast will;
34:   And, if thou canst not worship steadfastly,
35:   Work for Me, toil in works pleasing to Me!
36:   For he that laboureth right for love of Me
37:   Shall finally attain! But, if in this
38:   Thy faint heart fails, bring Me thy failure! find
39:   Refuge in Me! let fruits of labour go,
40:   Renouncing hope for Me, with lowliest heart,
41:   So shalt thou come; for, though to know is more
42:   Than diligence, yet worship better is
43:   Than knowing, and renouncing better still.
44:   Near to renunciation--very near--
45:   Dwelleth Eternal Peace!
46: 
47:   Who hateth nought
48:   Of all which lives, living himself benign,
49:   Compassionate, from arrogance exempt,
50:   Exempt from love of self, unchangeable
51:   By good or ill; patient, contented, firm
52:   In faith, mastering himself, true to his word,
53:   Seeking Me, heart and soul; vowed unto Me,--
54:   That man I love! Who troubleth not his kind,
55:   And is not troubled by them; clear of wrath,
56:   Living too high for gladness, grief, or fear,
57:   That man I love! Who, dwelling quiet-eyed,[FN#25]
58:   Stainless, serene, well-balanced, unperplexed,
59:   Working with Me, yet from all works detached,
60:   That man I love! Who, fixed in faith on Me,
61:   Dotes upon none, scorns none; rejoices not,
62:   And grieves not, letting good or evil hap
63:   Light when it will, and when it will depart,
64:   That man I love! Who, unto friend and foe
65:   Keeping an equal heart, with equal mind
66:   Bears shame and glory; with an equal peace
67:   Takes heat and cold, pleasure and pain; abides
68:   Quit of desires, hears praise or calumny
69:   In passionless restraint, unmoved by each;
70:   Linked by no ties to earth, steadfast in Me,
71:   That man I love! But most of all I love
72:   Those happy ones to whom 'tis life to live
73:   In single fervid faith and love unseeing,
74:   Drinking the blessed Amrit of my Being!
75: 
76:   HERE ENDETH CHAPTER XII. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA,
77:   Entitled "Bhaktiyog,"
78:   Or"The Book of the Religion of Faith."

records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Arjuna.
  Lord! of the men who serve Thee--true in heart--
  As God revealed; and of the men who serve,
  Worshipping Thee Unrevealed, Unbodied, Far,
  Which take the better way of faith and life?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.1 Arjuna said Those devotees who, ever steadfast, thus worship Thee and those also who worship the imperishable and the unmanifested which of them are better versed in Yoga?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.1 "Arjuna asked: My Lord! Which are the better devotees who worship Thee, those who try to know Thee as a Personal God, or those who worship Thee as Impersonal and Indestructible?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.1 Arjuna said Those devotees who, being thus ever dedicated, meditate on You, and those again (who meditate) on the Immutable, the Unmanifested-of them, who are the best experiencers of yoga [(Here) yoga means samadhi, spiritual absorption.] ?

records.sanskrit:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.2 The Blessed Lord said Those who, fixing their mind on Me, worship Me, ever steadfast and endowed with supreme faith, are the best in Yoga in My opinion.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.2 Lord Shri Krishna replied: Those who keep their minds fixed on Me, who worship Me always with unwavering faith and concentration; these are the very best.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.2 The Blessed Lord said Those who meditate on Me by fixing their minds on Me with steadfast devotion (and) being endowed with supreme faith-they are considered to be the most perfect yogis according to Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.4 Having restrained all the senses, even-minded everywhere, intent on the welfare of all beings verily they also come unto Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.4 Subduing their senses, viewing all conditions of life with the same eye, and working for the welfare of all beings, assuredly they come to Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.4 By fully controlling all the organs and always being even-minded, they, engaged in the welfare of all beings, attain Me alone.

arnold.content:

  To reach th' Unmanifest That viewless path

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.5 Greater is their trouble whose minds are set on the unmanifested; for the goal; the unmanifested, is very hard for the embodied to reach.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.5 But they who thus fix their attention on the Absolute and Impersonal encounter greater hardships, for it is difficult for those who possess a body to realise Me as without one.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.5 For them who have their minds attached to the Unmanifested the struggle is greater; for, the Goal which is the Unmanifest is attained with difficulty by the embodied ones.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.8 Fix thy mind in Me only, thy intellect in Me, (then) thou shalt no doubt live in Me alone hereafter.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.9 If thou art unable to fix thy mind steadily on Me, then by the Yoga of constant practice do thou seek to reach Me, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.9 But if thou canst not fix thy mind firmly on Me, then, My beloved friend, try to do so by constant practice.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.9 If, however, you are unable to establish the mind steadily on Me, then, O Dhananjaya, seek to attain Me through the Yoga of Practice.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.10 If thou art unable to practise even this Abhyasa Yoga, be thou intent on doing actions for My sake; even by doing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.10 And if thou are not strong enough to practise concentration, then devote thyself to My service, do all thine acts for My sake, and thou shalt still attain the goal.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.10 If you are unable even to practise, be intent on works for Me. By undertaking works for Me as well, you will attain perfection. [Identity with Brahman.]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.12 Better indeed is knowledge than practice; than knowledge meditation is better; than meditation the renunciation of the fruits of actions: peace immediately follows renunciation.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.14 He who is ever content, who is a yogi, who has self-control, who has firm conviction, who has dedicated his mind and intellect to Me-he who is such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.15 He by whom the world is not agitated and who cannot be agitated by the world, and who is freed from joy, anger, fear and anxiety he is dear to Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.15 He who does not harm the world, and whom the world cannot harm, who is not carried away by any impulse of joy, anger or fear, such a one is My beloved.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.15 He, too, owing to whom the world is not disturbed, and who is not disturbed by the world, who is free from joy, impatience, fear and anxiety, is dear to Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.16 He who expects nothing, who is pure, watchful, indifferent, unruffled, and who renounces all initiative, such a one is My beloved.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.16 He who has no desires, who is pure, who is dextrous, who is impartial, who is free from fear, who has renounced every undertaking-he who is (such) a devotee of Mine is dear to Me.

records.sanskrit:
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।
शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥
records.iast:
yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati
śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Who, fixed in faith on Me,
  Dotes upon none, scorns none; rejoices not,
  And grieves not, letting good or evil hap
  Light when it will, and when it will depart,
  That man I love!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.17 He who neither rejoices, nor hates, nor grieves, nor desires, renouncing good and evil, and who is full of devotion, is dear to Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.17 He who is beyond joy and hate, who neither laments nor desires, to whom good and evil fortunes are the same, such a one is My beloved.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.17 He who does not rejoice, does not fret, does not lament, does not hanker; who gives up good and bad, who is filled with devotion-he is dear to Me.

records.sanskrit:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥
records.iast:
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Who, unto friend and foe
  Keeping an equal heart, with equal mind
  Bears shame and glory; with an equal peace
  Takes heat and cold, pleasure and pain; abides
  Quit of desires,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: Shri Purohit Swami did not comment on this sloka

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: Swami Gambirananda did not comment on this sloka

records.sanskrit:
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित्।
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
records.iast:
tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yena kenacit
aniketaḥ sthiramatirbhaktimānme priyo naraḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
hears praise or calumny
  In passionless restraint, unmoved by each;
  Linked by no ties to earth, steadfast in Me,
  That man I love!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.19 He to whom censure and praise are eal, who is silent, content with anything, homeless, of a steady mind, and full of devotion that man is dear to Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.19 Who is indifferent to praise and censure, who enjoys silence, who is contented with every fate, who has no fixed abode, who is steadfast in mind, and filled with devotion, such a one is My beloved.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.19 The person to whom denunciation and praise are the same, who is silent, content with anything, homeless, steady-minded, and full of devotion is dear to Me.

records.sanskrit:
ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते।
श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥
records.iast:
ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate
śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktāste.atīva me priyāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But most of all I love
  Those happy ones to whom 'tis life to live
  In single fervid faith and love unseeing,
  Drinking the blessed Amrit of my Being!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 12.20 They verily who follow this immortal Dharma (law or doctrine) as described above, endowed with faith, regarding Me as their supreme goal, they, the devotees, are exceedingly dear to Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 12.20 Verily those who love the spiritual wisdom as I have taught, whose faith never fails, and who concentrate their whole nature on Me, they indeed are My most beloved."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 12.20 But [Tu (but) is used to distinguish those who have attained the highest Goal from the aspirants.-Tr.] those devotees who accept Me as the supreme Goal, and with faith seek for this ambrosia [M.S.'s reading is dharmamrtam-nectar in the form of virtue. Virtue is called nectar because it leads to Immortality, or because it is sweet like nectar.] which is indistinguishable from the virtues as stated above, they are very dear to Me.
